newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena confident Swissair will remain partner.
newsitem.headline: Sabena confident Swissair will remain partner.

text.p: Belgium's Sabena said on Monday the airline was on course for a breakeven result in 1998, adding its major shareholder Swissair had no problems with its restructuring programme and would continue to back it.

"We are very confident that by the end of June and the end of the year we will be in line with the budget. We are confident we will reach our goals and that...Swissair will certainly continue to cooperate with us," chief executive officer Paul Reutlinger told Reuters after a briefing for journalists.
Sabena, 49.5 percent owned by SAirGroup, the holding company which includes the Swiss airline, had 1996 consolidated loss after provisions of 8.87 billion Belgian francs.
After the news of the loss SAirGroup decided to write down fully its Sabena stake. It had also said it would assess its cooperation with Sabena at the end of June.
SAirGroup had warned Sabena would have to be in line with its budget for the cooperation to continue.
Sabena is aiming for a modest 1997 consolidated loss, breakeven in 1998 and profit from 1999.
"With these figures I do not think Swissair is going to change its opinion," Reutlinger said at the briefing.
